## Question 1 · B

Primary skill [1.1.2](../topic-guides/data-movement.md#batch-ingestion-by-source-and-destination) · also [2.1.4](../topic-guides/data-movement.md#batch-ingestion-by-source-and-destination), [1.1.3](../topic-guides/data-movement.md#manifests-and-incremental-loads)

A file share moved to S3 on a schedule with incremental transfer is DataSync.

- **A.** Incorrect. Transfer Family receives files from clients over SFTP. It does not pull from an NFS share on a schedule.
- **B.** Correct. DataSync copies changed files from NFS to S3 on a schedule and verifies integrity.
- **C.** Incorrect. DMS migrates databases. It does not read file shares.
- **D.** Incorrect. AppFlow connects SaaS applications, not on-premises file shares.

## Question 2 · C

Primary skill [2.1.3](../topic-guides/databases.md#memorydb-elasticache-dynamodb-and-vector-stores) · also [2.1.1](../topic-guides/databases.md#cost-latency-and-operational-trade-offs)

Microsecond reads plus durability, with no separate database, is MemoryDB.

- **A.** Incorrect. This works but adds a second system, and the cache is not the durable copy.
- **B.** Incorrect. DynamoDB gives single-digit millisecond reads, not microsecond reads.
- **C.** Correct. MemoryDB serves microsecond reads from memory and keeps data durable with a Multi-AZ transaction log.
- **D.** Incorrect. A warehouse is built for scans, not microsecond single-key lookups.

## Question 3 · A

Primary skill [3.1.3](../topic-guides/apis-and-sdks.md#aws-sdk-clients-pagination-and-errors) · also [3.1.4](../topic-guides/emr.md#operational-choices-on-emr-on-ec2)

SDK list operations are paginated. Use paginators to read every page.

- **A.** Correct. List calls return at most 1,000 keys per response. A paginator follows the continuation tokens.
- **B.** Incorrect. S3 caps each list response at 1,000 keys regardless of MaxKeys.
- **C.** Incorrect. S3 Select queries the contents of one object. It does not list objects.
- **D.** Incorrect. This is indirect, slow, and does not give a reliable list of keys.

## Question 4 · D

Primary skill [4.2.5](../topic-guides/governance.md#rbac-iam-abac-and-lf-tags) · also [4.2.6](../topic-guides/security.md#least-privilege-policy-examples-and-tests)

Attribute-based access control scales with tags instead of new policies.

- **A.** Incorrect. One policy per project is the maintenance burden the team wants to avoid.
- **B.** Incorrect. Groups still need one policy per project, and roles are preferred over users.
- **C.** Incorrect. The list must be edited every time a person or project changes.
- **D.** Correct. One policy compares tags, so new projects work by tagging, with no policy changes.

## Question 5 · C

Primary skill [1.1.3](../topic-guides/data-movement.md#manifests-and-incremental-loads) · also [2.3.1](../topic-guides/redshift.md#copy-staging-and-unload)

A manifest makes a batch load exact and fail-safe.

- **A.** Incorrect. A delay guesses at timing and still does not guarantee all 48 files are present.
- **B.** Incorrect. Smaller files speed the load but do nothing to ensure completeness.
- **C.** Correct. A manifest names the exact files, and COPY fails if a listed file is missing.
- **D.** Incorrect. The catalog does not control which files COPY loads from a prefix.

## Question 6 · A

Primary skill [2.2.6](../topic-guides/catalog-and-unified-studio.md#publish-an-asset-and-approve-subscriptions) · also [4.5.6](../topic-guides/catalog-and-unified-studio.md#project-subscriptions-and-fulfillment)

Business meaning, ownership, and access requests belong in a business catalog.

- **A.** Correct. SageMaker Catalog is a business catalog with definitions, ownership, and access workflows.
- **B.** Incorrect. A crawler infers technical schema. It cannot supply business meaning or approvals.
- **C.** Incorrect. This is manual, unsearchable across tools, and not tied to actual permissions.
- **D.** Incorrect. LF-Tags manage permissions, not discovery, definitions, or an approval workflow.

## Question 7 · A, D

Primary skill [3.3.7](../topic-guides/monitoring.md#cloudwatch-log-groups-retention-and-queries) · also [4.4.2](../topic-guides/monitoring.md#cloudwatch-log-groups-retention-and-queries)

Log groups keep data forever by default. Fix existing groups and set retention where new groups are created.

- **A.** Correct. Retention removes events older than the period from existing groups.
- **B.** Incorrect. The class cannot change after creation, and it does not set retention.
- **C.** Incorrect. Lambda and Glue recreate the groups, which again keep data forever.
- **D.** Correct. Groups defined in templates start with the right retention instead of the default.
- **E.** Incorrect. An alarm reports growth but does not set retention.

## Question 8 · C

Primary skill [4.1.3](../topic-guides/security.md#secrets-manager-and-parameter-store) · also [4.2.2](../topic-guides/security.md#secrets-manager-and-parameter-store)

Automatic credential rotation for databases is Secrets Manager.

- **A.** Incorrect. Parameter Store has no built-in rotation, so someone must maintain the script.
- **B.** Incorrect. Environment variables do not rotate, and changing them means redeploying the job.
- **C.** Correct. Secrets Manager rotates Aurora credentials automatically, and the job always reads the current value.
- **D.** Incorrect. IAM users do not hold database passwords, and this does not change the database login.

## Question 9 · D

Primary skill [1.1.5](../topic-guides/orchestration.md#schedules-time-zones-and-backfills) · also [3.1.9](../topic-guides/orchestration.md#eventbridge-rules-scheduler-and-pipes)

EventBridge Scheduler supports cron expressions in a named time zone.

- **A.** Incorrect. UTC cron does not shift for daylight saving, so the run time moves by an hour twice a year.
- **B.** Incorrect. Lambda stops after 15 minutes and this design is fragile.
- **C.** Incorrect. A rate expression cannot target a time of day or skip weekends.
- **D.** Correct. Scheduler supports time zones, so the run stays at 06:15 local time all year.

## Question 10 · A, D

Primary skill [2.3.6](../topic-guides/s3.md#replication-version-recovery-and-restore-testing) · also [2.3.4](../topic-guides/s3.md#versioned-deletes-and-dynamodb-ttl-comparison)

A replication time objective is RTC. Versioning is required for replication and gives overwrite recovery.

- **A.** Correct. RTC replicates 99.9% of objects within 15 minutes, with a second copy in another Region.
- **B.** Incorrect. This speeds uploads over long distances. It does not create a copy.
- **C.** Incorrect. This changes storage class only and makes recovery slower.
- **D.** Correct. Replication requires versioning, and versions allow recovery from overwrites.
- **E.** Incorrect. A weekly copy cannot meet a 15-minute objective.

Primary skill [3.1.6](../topic-guides/analysis-and-data-prep.md#databrew-recipes-and-unified-studio-preparation) · also [3.2.2](../topic-guides/analysis-and-data-prep.md#profile-validate-and-correct-a-batch)

No-code, repeatable cleaning steps fit DataBrew recipes.

- **A.** Incorrect. This requires coding, which the analysts cannot do.
- **B.** Correct. DataBrew offers visual transforms saved as reusable recipes and run by scheduled jobs.
- **C.** Incorrect. This still requires SQL, and manual edits invite errors.
- **D.** Incorrect. Calculated fields affect a dashboard, not a reusable cleaned dataset.

Private S3 access from a VPC is a gateway endpoint, and aws:SourceVpce restricts the bucket to it.

- **A.** Incorrect. This adds internet routing that the design avoids.
- **B.** Correct. The gateway endpoint gives the jobs a private route to S3.

- **D.** Incorrect. This does not give the jobs a route to S3 or restrict the source of requests.
- **E.** Incorrect. Acceleration uses edge locations over the internet, and TLS does not restrict the source.

## Question 13 · A

Primary skill [1.1.6](../topic-guides/orchestration.md#s3-events-and-eventbridge-routing) · also [1.3.2](../topic-guides/orchestration.md#queues-backpressure-retries-and-recovery)

EventBridge decouples the bucket from consumers. Add rules, not bucket settings.

- **A.** Correct. EventBridge rules filter by prefix, and new rules can add subscribers without touching the bucket.
- **B.** Incorrect. This works for one target, but each new subscriber means editing the bucket notification.
- **C.** Incorrect. Polling adds delay and cost, and listing can miss or repeat objects.
- **D.** Incorrect. Trail files arrive minutes later and require parsing.

## Question 14 · D

Primary skill [2.4.3](../topic-guides/data-modeling.md#dms-schema-conversion-and-manual-action-items) · also [1.1.2](../topic-guides/data-movement.md#batch-ingestion-by-source-and-destination)

Heterogeneous migrations need schema conversion and data replication, as two steps.

- **A.** Incorrect. Database files are engine-specific and cannot be attached to a different engine.
- **B.** Incorrect. Crawlers do not convert stored procedures, and Glue jobs do not replicate ongoing changes.
- **C.** Incorrect. DMS moves rows but does not convert stored procedures or report what needs manual work.
- **D.** Correct. Schema conversion handles structure and code. Replication moves and syncs rows until cutover.

## Question 15 · C

Primary skill [3.2.1](../topic-guides/analysis-and-data-prep.md#quicksight-dashboards-and-databrew-profiling) · also [3.2.3](../topic-guides/sql-patterns.md#athena-and-redshift-queries-and-views)

Fast dashboards over data that changes once a day fit SPICE with a scheduled refresh.

- **A.** Incorrect. Each dashboard view still sends queries to Athena.
- **B.** Incorrect. This is not an interactive dashboard.
- **C.** Correct. SPICE serves dashboards from memory, and a daily refresh matches the data's update schedule.
- **D.** Incorrect. OpenSearch fits search and log analytics, not BI dashboards over warehouse-style tables.

Always follow the identity that runs the work, which for Glue is the job's execution role.

- **A.** Incorrect. Starting a job only needs glue:StartJobRun. The job itself does not run as the developer.
- **B.** Correct. Glue assumes the execution role, so that role needs S3 and any KMS permissions.
- **C.** Incorrect. Jobs use the execution role you assign, not a service-linked role, for data access.
- **D.** Incorrect. The bucket policy or IAM policy grants access. The root user is not involved.

Private workloads that need a fixed public source IP go through a NAT gateway with an Elastic IP.

- **A.** Incorrect. Interface endpoints serve AWS services and PrivateLink providers, not an arbitrary internet API.
- **B.** Incorrect. Glue manages its network interfaces in private subnets. You cannot attach public IPs to them.
- **C.** Incorrect. Gateway endpoints only route to S3 or DynamoDB.
- **D.** Correct. All outbound traffic leaves through the NAT gateway's fixed Elastic IP, which the partner allowlists.

## Question 19 · D

Primary skill [3.4.4](../topic-guides/analysis-and-data-prep.md#random-and-stratified-sampling) · also [3.4.3](../topic-guides/data-quality.md#profile-drift-and-reconcile-counts)

Random samples miss rare groups. Stratify by the group you need to see.

- **A.** Incorrect. A larger random sample still includes very few rows from the small supplier.
- **B.** Incorrect. Arrival order is not random and may still skip the small supplier.
- **C.** Incorrect. This guarantees the small supplier is never checked.
- **D.** Correct. Stratified sampling draws from each group, so small groups are represented.

"Encrypted before it leaves" means client-side encryption.

- **A.** Incorrect. SSE-KMS encrypts after the data reaches S3, not before it leaves the partner.
- **B.** Correct. Data is encrypted in the partner's environment before transit, so it travels and lands encrypted.
- **C.** Incorrect. This enforces TLS in transit, but S3 still receives the plaintext file.
- **D.** Incorrect. This protects data at rest after arrival. It is not encryption before transit.

Throttling below table limits with one dominant key is a hot partition.

- **A.** Correct. Write sharding spreads one hot key across partitions so no single partition exceeds its limit.
- **B.** Incorrect. Table capacity is not the limit. One partition key exceeds what a partition can serve.
- **C.** Incorrect. The index has the same hot key and adds more writes.
- **D.** Incorrect. Retries hide the symptom and add latency without fixing the hot key.

Primary skill [2.1.6](../topic-guides/redshift.md#redshift-and-rds-transactions-locks-and-contention) · also [2.3.1](../topic-guides/redshift.md#copy-staging-and-unload)

Serializable conflicts between writers are solved by serializing them, for example with LOCK, or by retrying.

- **A.** Incorrect. Maintenance improves performance but does not prevent conflicting writes.
- **B.** Incorrect. Distribution does not affect transaction conflicts.
- **C.** Correct. An explicit lock makes the second job wait instead of conflicting.
- **D.** Incorrect. More memory does not prevent two transactions conflicting.

Distribute large tables on their common join key. Small dimensions can go to every node.
